scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual meter reads during Aug-Sep 2026 was 88%, below the 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: The billing-db tariff change log shows zero tariff-change records, i.e. no tariff changes were logged.

F-03.statement: Of 3025 disputed bills in billing-db, 1240 (41%) are read_type=ESTIMATED and 1785 (59%) are read_type=ACTUAL.

F-04.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-05.statement: crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly reports 610 (Jun-2026), 590 (Jul-2026), 1180 (Aug-2026), 1260 (Sep-2026) disputes, showing ticket volume roughly doubled starting in August 2026.

F-06.statement: route-log.lagging_routes query identifies 14 routes with below-target completion; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-07.statement: Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read-type bills, 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read before cutoff but were rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 (4.5%) had no AMI read received at all.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a response-handling capacity/speed problem; bills are largely correct and faster/automated ticket answering would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August (e.g., estimate-substitution logic) started producing incorrect bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI (vendor MDMS) read delivery degraded since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reading delivery (MeterWorks) degraded since August (missed/late reads), increasing estimated bills and disputes.

H-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field staffing shortfall is the underlying cause of missed/late manual reads, which in turn drives estimate substitution and bill disputes.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: Most disputed bills (59%, 1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL read type, suggesting the dispute surge is substantially driven by errors in how actual meter reads are processed/billed (e.g. rate/calculation or import-validation issues), not by estimate substitution from read failures.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and disputes, independent of AMI delivery or field-read failure.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual meter reads was 88% against a 95% target during the Aug-Sep 2026 dispute surge window, covering 9200 accounts, indicating a measurable shortfall in manual read collection during that period.

Still shows: field route completion for manual meter reads was 88% against a 95% target in Aug-Sep 2026, across 9200 accounts — a real shortfall in manual read collection. No longer means: per E-11, 95.5% of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills are AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import (not missing manual reads), so this route-completion shortfall cannot be shown to contribute to the ESTIMATED-dispute population as PD-1's premise (PR-CHAIN-6) claimed.

Billing-db's tariff change log contains zero records, meaning no tariff changes were logged that could explain altered bill amounts; this narrows (but does not confirm) causes of the dispute surge by eliminating tariff changes as a factor.

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (41%/59% of 3025 disputed bills), so most disputes involve bills generated from an actual meter read, not an estimated substitute. This means estimate-substitution failure (from AMI or field-read degradation) can at most account for a minority of the disputed-bill population; something else is producing wrong/disputed bills on actual reads.

Still shows: of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) are read_type=ESTIMATED and 1785 (59%) are read_type=ACTUAL — the raw split is unchanged. No longer means: the ESTIMATED minority can be attributed to estimate-substitution from AMI/field-read delivery failure or degradation, since E-11 reveals that population is instead dominated (95.5%) by billing-import rejection of valid AMI reads, so route completion (E-01) is not a viable explanatory mechanism for any meaningful share of it.

Across 2440 dispute tickets, median response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA. This shows ticket response handling is currently meeting its speed target, not breaching it.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, a non-authoritative stakeholder, claims no tariff change occurred this year; this agrees in direction with E-02's authoritative tariff_change_log finding of zero records for Aug-Sep 2026, but as an UNVERIFIED, NOT_APPLICABLE-completeness interview statement it adds no new evidentiary weight beyond corroborating that log.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, potentially biased toward staffing explanations) claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July causes late routes, which in turn produces estimated bills for affected customers. This is an unverified causal claim that offers a candidate mechanism behind the route-completion shortfall already observed (E-01), but it is not corroborated by any authoritative record here.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows ticket counts stable around 590-610/month in Jun-Jul 2026 then jumping to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep 2026 — roughly a 2x step increase that begins precisely in August. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the dispute surge itself but says nothing about which upstream mechanism (reads, billing rules, response handling) is causing it.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility (ORG-UTIL) may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) at the time of execution — this is a procedural/authorization fact, not evidence about the dispute surge's root cause, and it corroborates the already-encoded K-DISPATCH human-approval control on push_route_update.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query returns 14 individual routes below target, with a sample route (R-00) at 0.70 completion — this is route-level granularity underlying the aggregate 88% completion already captured in E-01, not new information about cause.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, ORG-AMI) states that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471. If accurate, this would resolve the access-pending blocker on the mdms-export tool (DA-MDMS), enabling the previously blocked AMI read-event query, but it is an unverified vendor-side claim, not confirmed by any authoritative mdms-export record.

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read-type bills (matching E-03's ESTIMATED count), mdms-export's own read-event log shows 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before the billing cutoff but were rejected during billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 (4.5%) genuinely had no AMI read received. This means the dominant cause of estimate substitution in this population is a billing-import validation rejection of valid AMI reads, not AMI delivery failure or missed manual field reads.

U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific defect in billing import/validation processing of ACTUAL-read bills (e.g. a rule change) is producing the incorrect/disputed bills?
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation should target a billing-config rule fix versus another mechanism; blocks any future bill-correction design.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-config's import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) and cross-reference change timestamps/accounts against the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills (E-03).
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Do not design or deploy any automated bill-correction logic; continue manual Billing Operations review of ACTUAL-read disputes until the defect is confirmed.

U-AMI-READ-DATA-UNAVAILABLE.question: Does AMI/MDMS read delivery contribute to the ACTUAL-read billing errors, given MDMS export access is currently vendor-pending?
U-AMI-READ-DATA-UNAVAILABLE.decision_impact: If AMI delivery is implicated, remediation may require vendor coordination rather than a pure billing-config fix.
U-AMI-READ-DATA-UNAVAILABLE.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (mdms-export is currently DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING per recovery log) and query AMI read events for the disputed-ACTUAL-read accounts.
U-AMI-READ-DATA-UNAVAILABLE.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db-based analysis of ACTUAL-read disputes (E-03) without assuming AMI involvement; treat the AMI-read-failure hypothesis as unresolved.
U-AMI-READ-DATA-UNAVAILABLE.resolution: MDMS export access is now functioning and shows that for the disputed ESTIMATED population, AMI read delivery itself largely succeeded (1184/1240 reads received before cutoff) but was rejected at billing import for high consumption; AMI delivery degradation is therefore not the driver here, though the ACTUAL-read-type dispute bucket (59%) is not covered by this query.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the claimed field reader staffing shortfall (SH-FIELD, E-06) explain the route-completion shortfall (E-01), and how much of the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute share does it account for?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether push_route_update scope should target staffing-driven route reprioritization versus another cause of the completion shortfall.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Cross-reference MeterWorks staffing records with route-log completion data (E-01) to size the staffing shortfall's contribution versus other causes of the 88% completion rate.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat route-completion remediation as independent of the ACTUAL-read billing defect investigation; do not attribute the full dispute surge to staffing.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Is 'dispute volume back to pre-August baseline' a valid sole success measure, or could some disputes reflect legitimate billing corrections rather than errors?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If a share of disputes are legitimate corrections, the DISPUTE_VOLUME_BASELINE target/threshold would need adjustment.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Review a sample of resolved dispute tickets to classify how many reflect genuine billing errors versus legitimate corrections, before fixing the baseline target.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use the pre-August ~600/month level as a provisional target only, flagged as unvalidated until ticket classification is reviewed.
